thoughts.title: Research explored
thoughts.summary: Perovskite/polymer UV sensing and thin-film interface questions.
thoughts.label: Completed + current
thoughts.text: My completed work focused on fluorescent CsPbBr3@Cs4PbBr6/PU perovskite/polymer nanocomposites and their use in a self-powered UV-sensing device. I am now working on ferroelectric switching and interfacial charge retention in thin-film systems, where electrical behaviour and interfaces become the central questions.
thoughts.note: I like research where a material property becomes a measurable device behaviour, and where the interesting part is understanding why that behaviour appears.

thoughts.title: Tools & methods
thoughts.summary: Fabrication, characterisation, electrical measurements and analysis.
thoughts.label: Tools I already use
thoughts.text: My experimental toolkit includes thin-film and nanomaterial fabrication, XRD with Rietveld refinement, SEM, AFM, UV-Vis-NIR absorption and Tauc analysis, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, P-E hysteresis, PUND and DC probe-station measurements. I use Python and OriginPro for analysis, and I have experience with DFT through Quantum ESPRESSO.
thoughts.note: I want computation to become part of how I ask the next experimental question, not just a separate skill that sits beside the lab work.

thoughts.title: Current direction
thoughts.summary: Semiconductor materials, interfaces, sensing and computation.
thoughts.label: Future direction
thoughts.text: I want to move deeper into semiconductor materials and interfaces while keeping the experimental grounding that taught me how real materials behave. Sustainable technology, low-carbon energy and sensing remain important anchors, especially where a materials problem connects to a practical environmental or technological constraint.
thoughts.noteLabel: The direction I am trying to build
thoughts.note: Experimental enough to know what is real. Computational enough to ask better questions. Curious enough to keep moving toward harder materials problems.
